instruction: Make the title text bold and italic, and set the slide background color to blue.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully changed content font size to 12, font color to orange, and slide background to red in LibreOffice Impress. Completed in 40 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select text in Impress, change font properties (size, color, bold, italic), change slide background color via properties panel.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests bold/italic formatting and a different background color (blue instead of red). Same interaction pattern but different properties.
metadata.explanation: Getter reads title bold/italic status and background color from saved pptx. Metric gives partial credit: 0.33 for bold, 0.33 for italic, 0.34 for blue background.

llm_judge_reasons: All three instruction requirements are verified: bold, italic, and blue background color with correct partial credit scoring (0.33 + 0.33 + 0.34 = 1.0).
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': expected.get('bg_color', '0000FF') directly accesses the rules dict.
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads it from disk, ensuring fresh state.
Minor concern: Getter uses slide.shapes[0] instead of slide.shapes.title to locate the title shape, which may not always be the title placeholder.

Minor concern: run.font.bold can return None (inherited from theme) rather than True, which would cause the 'is True' check to fail even if the text appears bold visually. However, when a user explicitly sets bold, python-pptx stores True, so this is acceptable for verifying user action.
Background color comparison uses 'in' operator (actual_bg.upper() contains expected), which is slightly loose but functionally correct for standard RGB hex strings.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using slide.shapes.title instead of slide.shapes[0] for more reliable title shape detection.
Consider checking run.font.bold is not False (rather than is True) to handle inherited bold from theme, or document that the check specifically validates explicit bold setting.
